verdict.rationale: Stripe documents a public API covering refunds, disputes, Checkout Sessions, idempotent retries, API-key authentication with least-privilege restricted keys, and backward-compatible monthly versioning. It also publishes OpenAPI spec files for generating clients, and a community user calls it 'the best API I've ever used'. Missing for 10: the pack has no first-party API reference overview page (only feature-level fragments), and the OpenAPI spec is not served at standard docs paths, only via the GitHub repo.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: You can programmatically manage disputes using the API. With the API, you can upload evidence, respond to disputes, and receive dispute events using webhooks.
You can issue refunds by using the Refunds API or the Dashboard
Stripe uses API keys to authenticate requests from your integration and determine which Stripe resources it can access.
Each monthly release includes only backward-compatible changes... You can safely upgrade to a new monthly release without breaking any existing code.
Use these files to generate SDKs or client libraries that support Stripe's API.
its the best API I've ever used. The documentation is clear and concise
